title: Micro head-to-head: luci-3q (4-bit) vs luci-3 fp16 - latency/quality tradeoffs
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact, operational note from the micro head-to-head we ran to decide whether to onboard luci-3 quantized (4-bit, called luci-3q) as a supported serving variant alongside the current luci-3 fp16 baseline. The goal: empirically evaluate latency/cost wins versus any measurable quality regressions on our customer prompt sets and a small human eval panel. This doc captures the experimental configuration, raw leaderboard-style summaries, visible regressions, and a recommended canary/rollback plan.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- luci-3q reduces median token latency by ~28% and estimated token compute cost by ~38% on our dedicated A100 pool.
- End-to-end quality (human-scored) shows a 1.8 point average drop on instruction-following prompts (out of 100) and negligible change on code/math prompts.
- Win/loss on pairwise head-to-head (n=1200 prompts): luci-3q wins 46%, ties 18%, loses 36% when compared to fp16.
- Recommendation: proceed with a staged canary (5% -> 20% -> 60%) for luci-3q for non-sensitive workloads and non-SLA customers while gating on prompt-set regression checks and automated hallucination detectors. Hold off on defaulting Hosted API traffic until we run one more 10k-prompt synthetic stress eval and a 100-human-eval expanded panel.

Experiment setup (short):
- Date range: 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-09
- Variants: luci-3 fp16 (baseline) vs luci-3q 4-bit (experimental)
- Hardware: Dedicated A100 pool (same instance size); comptime kernels compiled with our quantized path
- Batch policy: continuous batching with max_batch=8, dynamic padding enabled
- Prompt sets: three slices pulled from production historical traffic + adversarial subset:
  1) instruction-following (n=500): multi-turn instruction tasks
  2) code generation (n=300): function implementation + unit test prompts
  3) factual Q/A and math (n=300): closed-book retrieval turned off
- Human eval: 50 unique raters (mixed internal + contractor), each rated 200 prompts across slices for quality, helpfulness, and factuality (Likert 1-5), aggregated to 0-100 scale for this doc.

Automated metrics collected (per-prompt):
- latency_median_ms, latency_p95_ms, tokens_per_second, cost_per_k_token (est), perplexity (LM internal), safety_flag (binary), hallucination_score (heuristic), length_tokens, generation_termination_flags

Leaderboard (aggregated views) - condensed ASCII table:

Variant | Median Latency (ms) | P95 Latency (ms) | Est token cost | Human quality (0-100) | Win% (pairwise)
------- | ------------------- | ---------------- | -------------- | --------------------- | ----------------
luci-3 fp16 | 34.5 | 142 | $0.0120 /k | 86.7 | 54%
luci-3q (4-bit) | 24.9 | 118 | $0.0074 /k | 84.9 | 46%

Notes on the table: cost numbers are unit-estimates derived from measured GPU utilization and our cost model, not invoice numbers. Win% is pairwise aggregated across all prompt slices (ties counted separately).

Per-slice breakdown (highlights):
- Instruction-following (n=500): luci-3q shows median latency drop of 31%; human quality delta = -2.7 points (fp16 88.1 -> 85.4). Fail modes: occasional terse answers, tendency to omit clarifying follow-ups. Hallucination_score increased modestly (mean +0.12).
- Code generation (n=300): median latency drop 25%; human quality delta = -0.3 points (insignificant). Notable: luci-3q sometimes shortens generated comments but functional code passes unit tests at similar rate.
- Factual/math (n=300): median latency drop 28%; human quality delta = -0.4 points. Edge case: long-chain arithmetic (>6 steps) had slightly higher error rate with luci-3q but still within acceptable for non-SLA.

Representative win/loss matrix (pairwise categories) - counts out of 1200 comparisons:
- luci-3q wins: 552 (46%)
- ties: 216 (18%)
- luci-3q loses: 432 (36%)

Qualitative failure examples (selected prompts):
1) Instruction: "Summarize the following policy paragraph and suggest two clarifying questions."
   - fp16: thorough summary + 2 clarifying questions (good)
   - luci-3q: short summary, missed second clarifier (loss)
2) Code: "Implement function to parse ISO timestamps and edge-case DST transitions."
   - fp16: longer docstring and full edge-case handling
   - luci-3q: correct parse, slightly less exhaustive error handling (tie)
3) Factual: multi-hop question about historical timelines
   - fp16: correct chain, references
   - luci-3q: short chain, minor chronology mis-ordering (loss)

Statistical significance & notes:
- We ran bootstrap on human scores; the -1.8 point delta overall is statistically significant at p<0.05 on the instruction slice, but not significant on code/math slices.
- Latency reductions are robust across batch sizes and replicate runs (5 independent runs per config).

Operational impact & risk assessment:
- Upside: ~38% token compute savings is material for high-throughput customers and Dedicated pool sizing; lower latency improves tail experience for interactive products.
- Downside: small but measurable quality regressions on instruction-following prompts that could increase customer support incidents for some product flows (chat assistants, docs summarization).
- Security/safety: no increase in safety_flags observed, but hallucination heuristics rose slightly; recommend enabling stricter post-generation filters for any canary traffic.

Suggested canary rollout plan (recommended):
1) Internal-only: 0% live traffic; run expanded synthetic 10k prompt stress test and 100 human evaluator panel (duration 7 days) -> gating metric: instruction-slice human score drop must be <= 1.0 points relative to fp16.
2) Soft canary (non-SLA customers, opt-in): 5% of Eligible traffic, monitor 24/7 for 72h. Alert triggers: instruction human proxy metric delta > 2.5, hallucination_score +0.3, error_rate increase > 0.5%.
3) Broader canary: 20% for 7 days if soft canary passes.
4) Ramp to 60% with monitoring hooks and automated rollback on thresholds.

Gating checks and observability (what to monitor):
- Prompt-set regression job: run nightly with a stable set of 5k prompts including adversarial cases; produce diff reports (per-slice) and auto-open JIRA if regressions exceed thresholds.
- Evals dashboard: human_quality_estimate (proxy), median_latency, p95_latency, hallucination_score_trend, safety_flags by route.
- Cost dashboard: delta in GPU-hours and estimated token cost by customer tier.
- Tracing: sample token-level attention heatmaps for any prompt where hallucination_score spikes > baseline + 0.2.

Rollback and fallback strategies (pre-planned):
- Immediate rollback: traffic routing change to pin returning users to fp16; take luci-3q variant out of routing configs.
- Fallback model: if rollback fails for some infra reason, route to smaller fp16 variant or lower quantized variant candidate (kept as warm hot-standby).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there a quick quantization-retrain knob (mixed-precision middle layer) to recover the ~2.7 point loss on instruction tasks with minimal latency regression? (Action: priya to spike)
- Should we exclude luci-3q from Hosted API by default but allow explicit model param for advanced users? Need product input (action: product-hosted-api sync).
- Are there specific customer routes (e.g., embeddings-adjacent, classification) where luci-3q is categorically unacceptable? We need SRE to run longer tail tests.

Action items and owners:
- Expanded synthetic run (10k prompts): Ethan Chang (due 2026-07-16)
- 100-person human panel expansion: Liam O'Connor (contractor coordination) (due 2026-07-18)
- Product decision sync re: Hosted API opt-in vs default: Priya Nair + product-hosted-api (meeting 2026-07-13)
- Small quantization spike experiment: Priya Nair (due 2026-07-14)
- Create canary routing plan and alert thresholds in Console: eng-ops (ticket JIRA-OPS-1987)

Appendix (quick reproducibility notes):
- git ref: github.com/redwood-inference/luci @pr-487 (quant kernels)
- eval harness: rwi-eval-runner v2.3 (docker image sha256:abcd1234)
- config snippets: batch_max=8, kv_cache_prefetch=true, quantization-mode=4bit-dynamic

If you want the raw CSVs, latency histograms, or the human rater spreadsheets, ping me and I will upload them to the shared folder (they're large).

Decision recommendation (single line):
Approve staged canary for luci-3q for non-SLA, non-sensitive traffic with strict nightly prompt-set regression gating; delay default Hosted API exposure until post-expanded-eval results.
